 JOHOR BARU: A total of 207 schools in Johor have been identified as potential temporary relief centres (PPS) as the state prepares for possible floods during the upcoming Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examinations.
 State education and information committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the preparations were aimed at ensuring candidates would not miss their examinations due to flooding.
 He said the identified locations comprised 202 primary schools and five secondary schools, which could be opened as PPS if necessary.
 “Johor Education Department has also identified candidates who could be affected by floods, as well as alternative examination venues, particularly in Tangkak, Segamat and Kota Tinggi,” he said in a statement here on Wednesday (Nov 18).
 Dr Muhammad Naqib added coordination meetings involving relevant agencies had been held to ensure facilities and infrastructure were in good condition and ready for use when required.
 He said that schools had been instructed to monitor the circumstances of every candidate, including their home conditions and whether their travel routes to examination centres could be affected by floods.
 “Communication channels with parents will also be expanded to ensure updates could be shared promptly, while state Education Department and district education offices are prepared to provide assistance to affected candidates to help them reach their examination centres,” he added.
 He said the preparations were in line with the advice of Johor Mentri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi for all agencies to take early action and remain prepared for any eventuality.
 “The state government remains committed to safeguarding the people’s welfare particularly students sitting for these important examinations, and ensuring they can do so safely and without disruption from floods,” he said.
